steps.title: Web service - Domains and TLS
steps.subtitle: Passkeys bind to this exact host name: set the final one before anyone registers.

steps.title: Web service - Upstream
steps.subtitle: Point REVERSE_PROXY_HOST at Pocket ID's port 1411.

steps.title: HTTP - Client address for Pocket ID
steps.subtitle: Send BunkerWeb's view of the client, so a forged X-Forwarded-For never reaches the audit log or the app's limits.

steps.title: HTTP - API methods and upload size
steps.subtitle: Pocket ID uses PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS; uploads stop at 10 MiB, so 11m lets its own error through.

steps.title: HTTP - Request rate
steps.subtitle: The web app asks for the same URL up to 7 times in one second: 20r/s keeps it working and still caps floods.

steps.title: HTTP - Upstream error bodies
steps.subtitle: Pass Pocket ID's own JSON errors through: OIDC clients and the web app read them.

steps.title: Security - Bad behavior status codes
steps.subtitle: Pocket ID answers 401, 404 and 400 as part of normal use: keep them out of the ban counter.

steps.title: Security - Permissions-Policy for passkeys
steps.subtitle: BunkerWeb's default turns passkeys off; this copy allows publickey-credentials-create and -get for the site itself.

steps.title: Security - CRS exclusions for callback URLs and admin secrets
steps.subtitle: Path-scoped: LAN, loopback and IPv6 callback URLs, the SCIM endpoint, SMTP and LDAP bind passwords.
